interfaceText.detail1: Architectural breakdown of LSA isolation, LSASS process memory injection techniques, and Mimikatz SSP mitigation.
interfaceText.detail2: Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (LSASS) enforces local security policy. Attackers use Process Injection (T1055) or LSASS Memory Dump (T1003.001) to harvest NTLM hashes and Kerberos tickets. Enable Windows Defender Credential Guard (LsaCfgFlags=1) to isolate LSA secrets inside a Virtualization-based Security (VBS) container.
interfaceText.detail3: Critical Windows Security Event IDs for SOC Monitoring
interfaceText.detail4: Essential Event Tracing for Windows (ETW) Event IDs for threat detection.
interfaceText.detail5: Sigma & YARA Rule Authoring Best Practices
interfaceText.detail6: Offline rule writing guidelines for detecting malicious process creation and memory signatures.
interfaceText.detail7: Sigma rules standardize log detection logic across SIEMs. YARA rules evaluate binary memory or file byte sequences. Ensure condition selections avoid overly broad wildcards on common binaries (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) to minimize false positives.
interfaceText.detail8: Detected {count} failed login attempts in the past hour.
interfaceText.detail9: Unusual process turnover rate: {count} processes spawned/killed in one hour.
interfaceText.detail10: Process is maintaining {count} concurrent outbound connections.
interfaceText.detail17:
• Event ID 4688: New process created (Requires Audit Process Creation + Command Line Audit enabled).
• Event ID 4624 / 4625: Successful / Failed Logon attempts. LogonType 3 = Network, LogonType 10 = RemoteDesktop.
• Event ID 4768 / 4769: Kerberos TGT requested / Kerberos Service Ticket requested (Kerberoasting T1558.003).
• Sysmon Event ID 1: Process Creation with Hashes.
• Sysmon Event ID 3: Network Connection Initiated.
• Sysmon Event ID 13: Registry Value Set.
